programs.notes: Plan BH114P24, City Campus, full-time 4 years, intakes February and July, on campus. Plan rule: 27 core courses + 1 University Elective + 4 courses (48 credit points) from minors or electives = 32 courses of 12 credit points = 384. Year totals are 96 each (year 2: 84 core + 12 from minor or elective; years 3 and 4: 72 core + 24 each). The five minor/elective slots are placed by year as the plan states. Honours award level depends on weighted average mark. Guaranteed credit: Diploma of Building and Construction (Building) gives 96 credit points. A Singapore version under BH114 (search result) has been discontinued; not collected. Search-result summary mentioned AU$43,200 for 2026 on the apply page, but that figure is not in the saved apply page, so not recorded. Page mentions a separate ATAR of 65.65. No 3-year exit award stated.

course_list: Minor unit slot 1 (Building Compliance or Quantity Surveying)
programs.notes: Single campus: Footscray Park (page location), delivery mode In Person. Course structure: 384 credit points = 96 First Year Core + 240 Professional Core + 48 minor (Building Compliance or Quantity Surveying, the latter subject to enrolment numbers); 32 units of 12 credit points. Teaching uses the VU Block Model (page names it; semester blocks listed in intakes: Semester 1 Block 1 and Block 3, Semester 2 Block 1; Block 1 start 15 February 2027, Block 3 26 April 2027, Semester 2 Block 1 26 July 2027). The page does not state hours per credit point. First Year Core units listed without semester. Credit pathways: Diploma of Building and Construction (Building) gives 96 credit points (under 5 years experience) or 144 (over 5 years). Intakes shown are 2027. No 3-year exit award stated. Page states no minimum ATAR. A first-class honours rule applies (weighted average 60% years 1 to 3, 80% year 4, HD in NBC4006).

facts.text: AIB’s academic standards set no minimum years, hours, credit points or days of industry experience; duration must be consistent with the course outcomes and comply with the AQF.
